criteria.text: POST /opencode/providers/test accepts exactly the closed provider schema and validates provider ID, name, URL and unknown fields without reflecting the API key.
Endpoint policy permits HTTPS public endpoints and literal local HTTP addresses while blocking unsafe schemes, public HTTP, metadata/link-local, redirects and malformed URLs.
The server probes /models with bounded safe transport behavior and returns only sorted, deduplicated, capped model metadata with sanitized stable errors.
Testing persists nothing and does not call engine SDK auth.
PUT independently re-tests, stores an optional key only through auth.set, then uses schema-validated PATCH /global/config as the provider commit point.
If auth.set fails no config mutation occurs; if global config update fails the newly-created auth is removed and no provider config is persisted.
A successful global config update disposes provider instances and save returns 200 only when the real provider snapshot/catalog exposes every discovered model.
The route remains local-agent-only and is absent from hosted/cloud deployments.
Model Curation shows an accessible compact Add custom provider disclosure with named fields and a password API-key field.
Test connection exposes idle/testing/success/error states, exact count grammar, actionable sanitized errors and invalidates on any edit.
Save is enabled only for the exact successfully tested fields, repeats server validation, clears the secret/form, refreshes both catalogs and expands the usable provider group.
The UI retains keyboard, labels, 44px targets, live regions, no nested interactives, existing searches/auth/visibility behavior, and no renderer-held key after success.
A gated live test drives POST and PUT through sandbox API7398/engine7397, observes the provider in /agents/models/catalog/full, confirms no key in config, and proves the engine boot ID is unchanged.
A warm GET /config/providers followed by PATCH /global/config disposes the global instance and publishes the synthetic provider/model without a process restart.
criteria.reason: Focused fork probe passed 4/4, including warm-cache publication after the disposal event.

criteria.text: The installed v2 auth.remove cleans a newly-created credential only when global config update itself fails; successful global update is the commit point and is not deleted on later publication delay.
If publication remains delayed after a successful commit, return HTTP 202 pending; the UI clears the key, makes no connected claim, and offers Refresh models.
Pending refresh preserves the committed provider ID, refreshes full and shared-picker catalogs, resolves and expands when models appear, and otherwise retains a retryable pending state.
After PUT 200, either catalog refresh may fail without changing saved truth; the UI reports models could not be refreshed and retry runs both refreshes.
A test result is ignored if fields changed in flight, and all provider fields are disabled during save so submitted edits are not cleared accidentally.
Refresh models and provider disclosure targets are at least 44px, while provider-local search reaches 44px at narrow or coarse-pointer breakpoints and stays compact on desktop.
